uni31.title: ATM User-Network Interface Specification, Version 3.1 (UNI 3.1)
uni31.author: The ATM Forum (Chief Editor: G. Ratta, Bellcore)
uni31.quote: The Generic Cell Rate Algorithm (GCRA) is a Virtual Scheduling Algorithm or a continuous-state Leaky Bucket Algorithm as defined by the flowchart in Figure 3-15. ... The GCRA depends only on two parameters: the increment I and the Limit L. These parameters have been denoted by T and tau respectively in Annex 1 of I.371, but have been given more generic labels herein since the GCRA will be used in multiple instances. ... The two algorithms in Figure 3-15 are equivalent in the sense that for any sequence of cell arrival times, {ta(k), k >= 1} the two algorithms determine the same cells to be conforming and thus the same cells to be non-conforming. The two algorithms are easily compared if one notices that at each arrival epoch, ta(k), and after the algorithms have been executed, TAT = X + LCT. ... The capacity of the bucket (the upper bound on the counter) is L + I.
supports: GCRA is defined twice, as virtual scheduling and as continuous-state leaky bucket
the two versions are proven to mark the same cells non-conforming
TAT = X + LCT is the bridge between the two
the algorithm has exactly two parameters, increment I and limit L
uni31.notes: Two renditions sit in the same ATM Forum directory (af-uni-0010.002) and they are not the same document. The published specification is toc.pdf plus nine page-range PDFs; its title page reads 'ATM User-Network Interface Specification / Version 3.1 / September, 1994' and its Acknowledgements read 'the UNI 3.1 editing team led by Greg Ratta'. Every quote above was read there, in 049_103.pdf: GCRA is section 3.6.2.4.1 on pp. 77-79, and Figure 3-15 is captioned 'Equivalent versions of the Generic Cell Rate Algorithm' on p. 78. Other exact strings read in the published text: 'The maximum transfer rate for ATM layer data is 149.760 Mbps.', 'Each set consists of a sequence equivalent to 27 cells of 53 octets.' and 'The payload transmission rate for data cells is exactly 149.76 Mbps (155.52 * 26/27 = 149.76).' (2.4.3.2), plus 'yielding a transfer capacity for ATM cells of 149.760 Mbps' for the SONET STS-3c mapping (2.1.1.2.2.3); 'When cells from two or more ATM connections are multiplexed, cells of a given ATM connection may be delayed while cells of another ATM connection are being inserted at the output of the multiplexer.' and 'The upper bound on the “clumping” measure is called CDV Tolerance.' and '(R) A user shall explicitly or implicitly select a value for the CDV Tolerance at the public UNI for an ATM connection from a set of values supported by the network. Whether the set of values is to be standardized or to be determined by the network operator is for further study.' (3.6.2.4.2.4); 'A specific UPC mechanism may commit errors by taking policing actions on a compliant connection, e.g. the number of discarded cells of a compliant connection is more than the number of non-conforming cells according to the Traffic Contract.', 'Excessive policing actions of the UPC on a compliant connection are part of the overall Network Performance degradation.' and 'Safety margins may be provisioned depending upon the UPC algorithm to limit the degradation introduced by the UPC.' (3.6.3.2.3.2); and the published Preface, 'This version, UNI 3.1, of the interface specification has been created to bring The ATM Forum implementation agreements in line with the recent agreements in international standards'. The second rendition, uni-3.1.I.pdf and uni-3.1.II.pdf, is the pre-publication draft: every page carries the running header 'Draft of May 28, 1994', the title page reads 'Chief Editor - G. Ratta (Bellcore)' with 'gregra@cc.bellcore.com', the front matter is signed 'Greg Ratta, Chief Editor', and its Preface reads 'Part I of this version, UNI 3.1, of the interface specification has been created to bring The ATM Forum impelementation agreements in line with the recent agreements in international standards and reflects only the changes to UNI 3.0 necessary to achieve this' (the typo is in the original). That draft is a delta document and it enumerates every section UNI 3.1 changes - 3.4.4, 3.5.1, 4.2.3, 4.4.x, 4.6.2 and 5.x, all signalling, OAM and management. Section 3.6 is not among them, the string GCRA appears zero times in either draft part, and draft Part II adds three physical-layer interfaces only. So the rate-limiting text printed in UNI 3.1 is inherited UNI 3.0 (September 1993) material, not written for this revision.

i371.title: ITU-T Recommendation I.371 (03/93), Traffic control and congestion control in B-ISDN
i371.author: ITU-T Study Group XVIII
i371.quote: T and τ are the only parameters needed to define the virtual monitor algorithm. ... Two equivalent versions of this algorithm are shown: the virtual scheduling algorithm and the continuous state leaky bucket algorithm. In the first version, τ is expressed in units of time. In the second one, the leaky bucket capacity measured in units of time is equal to LB = T + τ.
supports: bucket capacity is the rate interval T plus the tolerance tau
the two equivalent versions are the ITU's, and predate the ATM Forum's UNI 3.1
the algorithm needs exactly two parameters, T and tau
i371.notes: Edition swapped to the contemporaneous one. The story is dated 1994, so the 03/2004 edition originally cited here was on the wrong side of it. I.371 (03/93) is the earliest edition ITU's own catalogue lists; its Foreword reads 'ITU-T Recommendation I.371 was prepared by the ITU-T Study Group XVIII (1988-1993) and was approved by the WTSC (Helsinki, March 1-12, 1993)'. Annex A is titled 'Peak cell rate cell monitor algorithms accounting for cell delay variation tolerance', pp. 20-21, and Figure A.1/I.371 is captioned 'Equivalent versions of the peak cell rate monitor algorithm' - the same two flowcharts UNI 3.1 reprints as Figure 3-15. Note the term 'Generic Cell Rate Algorithm' appears zero times in the 03/93 edition: the name is the ATM Forum's, and the ITU had adopted it by I.371 (08/96), which states 'The capacity of the bucket (the upper bound of the counter) is (T+τ).' The 03/2004 edition (approved 29 March 2004 by ITU-T Study Group 13) still prints it, in Annex A.2 on p. 87, as 'The capacity of the bucket (the upper bound of the counter) is (T + τ).' All three editions were opened. One mismatch worth knowing: UNI 3.1 cites this as 'Figure 1 in Annex 1 of I.371', which is not the published numbering (Annex A, Figure A.1) - the Forum was citing a draft.

rfc2697.title: RFC 2697, A Single Rate Three Color Marker
rfc2697.author: J. Heinanen, R. Guerin
rfc2697.quote: The srTCM meters a traffic stream and marks its packets according to three traffic parameters, Committed Information Rate (CIR), Committed Burst Size (CBS), and Excess Burst Size (EBS) ... The behavior of the Meter is specified in terms of its mode and two token buckets, C and E, which both share the common rate CIR. The maximum size of the token bucket C is CBS and the maximum size of the token bucket E is EBS.
supports: the ATM two-parameter bucket reappears in IP as rate plus two burst sizes
rfc2697.notes: Full text read at rfc-editor.org. Header block: 'Network Working Group J. Heinanen / Request for Comments: 2697 Telia Finland / Category: Informational R. Guerin / University of Pennsylvania / September 1999'. The first half of the quote is the Abstract; the two-bucket sentence is section 3, Metering, not section 1. Last page footer reads 'Heinanen & Guerin Informational [Page 6]'. A case-insensitive grep for 'atm' over the full text returns zero matches.

unverified: That J. S. Turner named the leaky bucket in 'New directions in communications (or which way to the information age?)', IEEE Communications Magazine 24(10):8-15, October 1986. The bibliographic record was confirmed via Crossref (DOI 10.1109/mcom.1986.1092946) but the paper is closed access and its text was never opened, so the attribution is not used in the prose or on any card.

That ITU-T I.371 was first published in 1991. ITU's own catalogue lists 03/93 as the earliest edition, the 03/93 Foreword names no predecessor, and no 1991 PDF is served. The 03/93, 08/96 and 03/2004 editions were opened directly; no 1991 date is claimed anywhere.

That UNI 3.0 (September 1993) is the ATM Forum document where this rate-limiting text first appears. UNI 3.0 itself was not opened - no copy is on the mirror that carries UNI 3.1. The inference is from UNI 3.1's own draft, which enumerates every section it changes and does not include 3.6.

Any currency figure for a carrier's cost of wrongly discarding a compliant customer's cells. UNI 3.1 books the damage as 'Network Performance degradation' and puts no price on it; no priced dispute was found, so no money figure appears in the prose or on a card. O9's money clause is unmet by design rather than by oversight.

That the ATM Forum Traffic Management working group, as a named body, settled the GCRA text. The specification credits individual contributors by subject area and does not name a traffic-management group.

The cell rate in the prose as a quoted figure. '353,000 verdicts a second, under three microseconds each' is arithmetic on two quoted UNI 3.1 numbers - 149,760,000 bits/s over 424 bits gives 353,207.5 cells/s and 2.83 microseconds - and the sentence shows the division rather than asserting a sourced figure.
